title: GPT 6.1 Terra: Features, Pricing, and Access (2026)
summary: GPT 6.1 Terra adds capabilities to automation workflows. See what's changed in this model and how it impacts your current automation setup.
body_markdown:
## Test GPT 6.1 Terra on automation tasks


That test is easy to run, and ours came out against the switch. **On 2026-10-26, Terra was slower and costlier per task than gpt-5.4-mini, so any case for it has to rest on quality.** This is a small, indicative test, not a benchmark.


> **On 2026-10-26, Terra was slower and costlier per task than gpt-5.4-mini, so any case for it has to rest on quality.


### How we scored GPT 6.1 Terra tasks


We ran Terra and openai/gpt-5.4-mini through[OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/openai/gpt-6.1-terra) on the same three jobs, so the results are directly comparable. Terra used default settings, which reason before answering.


The jobs were to sort a support ticket, pull fields from an invoice, and summarise an email thread. That makes their results directly comparable. We checked each output against a known answer.


With so few tasks, treat the gaps as a prompt to test your own workload, not as a verdict.


### Results, speed and cost per task


Terra's median time was 1 second for ticket sorting, 1.2 seconds for invoice fields and 2 seconds for the email summary, which means email summary processing takes twice as long as ticket sorting.


A step that must read and condense a long thread is therefore the one where Terra's reasoning delay is most visible.


Across the three tasks, **Terra's median was 1.2 seconds against 0.8** for gpt-5.4-mini, and its cost per task was $0.000256 against $0.000141.


Per task, that is about 1.8 times the cost, or **$2.56 against $1.41 for every 10,000 runs** .


That gap is small in absolute terms, so it only matters at high volume or where a workflow waits on each step. If your outputs are equally correct on both models, the cheaper one wins.
